purpose: Response-blind qualification of the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary Seagrass Monitoring Project as an independent test of Tampa quantitative early warning.
hypothesis: Among source-year transects with recorded Thalassia presence, lower quantitative Thalassia state predicts next-year recorded loss beyond space/time/effort.

source.program_name: Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary Seagrass Monitoring Project
source.stated_method: Fixed transect - (10) random .25m^2 quadrats; data reported at transect level; Braun-Blanquet score averaged across quadrats

required_before_data_access: explicit recorded-absence/zero semantics distinguishable from missing
publicly reproducible data source identity without selecting files after inspecting biological outcomes
stop_rule: If public metadata cannot establish all required semantics before biological data access, stop v1 pre-response.
no_rescue: Do not use biological data values to infer schema.
Do not treat missing or unreported cover as absence.
Do not change the endpoint from next-year recorded loss after data access.
Do not choose a different Florida Keys data file after observing Thalassia outcomes.
